intel.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs aiming to manufacture luxury fur garments, fur accessories, or fur home décor items.

intel.whatItMeans: This KBLI covers the manufacturing of all types of apparel made from knitted or crocheted fabrics, including sweaters, t-shirts, shirts, blouses, vests, coats, sleepwear, underwear, baby clothes, sportswear, swimwear, and accessories like hats and gloves (except socks). Essentially, it's the full range of ready-to-wear knitwear and crocheted clothing and gear.
intel.baliReality: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership. However, under Bali's current rules, low- and medium-low-risk KBLI like this one are subject to a moratorium that blocks new PMA companies; you cannot register a foreign-owned entity for this business in Bali until at least 13 May 2026.
intel.whoThisIsFor: Foreign fashion entrepreneurs or brands wanting to set up their own knitwear or crocheted apparel production in Indonesia.

intel.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of knitted or crocheted hosiery items like socks, tights, stockings, pantyhose, and medical compression stockings. It also includes making sol-free footwear from knitted or crocheted material.
intel.baliReality: While nationally this business is 100% open to foreign ownership, in Bali a PMA company currently cannot register this KBLI. An ongoing administrative moratorium blocks low- and medium-low risk business codes for foreign companies here (likely until mid-2026).
intel.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur planning to manufacture branded socks, stockings, or specialty medical hosiery in Indonesia.

intel.whatItMeans: This covers the tanning of animal hides and skins—after pre-tanning—using synthetic agents (like chromium) or vegetable-based methods to produce finished leathers such as wet blue, crust, suede, patent leather, laminated leather, and specialty skins like chamois or hair-on hides.
intel.baliReality: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open (100% foreign ownership). However, the Bali authority currently blocks PMA registration for this activity because it falls under the low/medium-low risk class moratorium, meaning a foreign-owned company cannot be established in Bali for leather tanning at this time.
intel.whoThisIsFor: This suits foreign entrepreneurs in leather goods manufacturing, fashion, or automotive interiors who want to control their raw material supply by running a tannery—but they must look outside Bali due to the current restriction.

intel.whatItMeans: This covers the process of dyeing or coloring leather that still has its fur or wool attached (e.g., sheepskin, shearling). The activity is specifically for treating furry hides used in finished leather goods like coats, bags, or footware.
intel.baliReality: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). However, in Bali the activity is currently blocked for foreign-owned companies due to a local moratorium that halts new PMA registrations for low and medium-low risk classes until 2026—so you cannot legally set up a foreign-owned dyeing workshop for furry leather on the island.
intel.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur with deep expertise in leather dyeing and a supply chain for furry hides, but who will need to base the operation outside Bali while this restriction remains.

intel.whatItMeans: This covers the preservation of raw animal hides and skins through methods like drying, salting, or pickling. It applies to large animal skins (cow, buffalo), small animal skins (sheep, goat), reptile skins (crocodile, snake, monitor lizard), fish skins (stingray, shark, snapper, eel), and other animal hides.
intel.baliReality: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). However, in Bali, a regional moratorium—in effect since mid-2024 and lasting at least until 13 May 2026—blocks PMA registration for low and medium-low risk business lines, which includes this KBLI. As a result, a foreigner cannot currently set up a leather preservation company in Bali.
intel.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur in the leather supply chain who wants to build a hide or skin preservation facility for export or to supply local tanneries and craft industries.

intel.whatItMeans: This sector covers manufacturing of animal equipment and accessories from leather or other materials—everything from saddles, harnesses, and collars to muzzles, whips, animal footwear, carry bags, and even pet clothing.
intel.baliReality: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. However, in Bali the picture is different: low/medium-low risk classifications are currently blocked by a moratorium effective until May 13, 2026. That means a PMA cannot obtain this activity on its Bali business license during the moratorium period.
intel.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs looking to manufacture premium leather or fabric accessories for pets and working animals.

intel.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing engineered wood panels like MDF, particle board, OSB, and honeycomb board—typically used in furniture, construction, and interior applications. It's a factory-scale production activity, not a simple woodworking workshop.
intel.baliReality: Nationally, this activity is open to 100% foreign ownership. However, due to Bali’s current moratorium on new PMA registrations for low and medium-low risk activities (in effect until 13 May 2026), you cannot register a foreign-owned company under this KBLI in Bali at this moment.
intel.whoThisIsFor: A foreign manufacturer aiming to set up a wood-panel production plant for export or B2B supply, who is willing to either wait for the Bali moratorium to lift or consider basing the facility outside Bali.

intel.whatItMeans: This activity covers making various leather and composition-leather goods not classified elsewhere—such as upholstery, decorative crafts (shadow puppets, lampshades), and machine parts like van belts and gaskets.
intel.baliReality: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership, but in Bali a local moratorium blocks new PMA registrations for low/medium-low-risk activities. As a result, a foreign-owned company cannot currently obtain this business license in Bali under this code.
intel.whoThisIsFor: A foreign artisan or manufacturer looking to produce niche leather goods for machinery or handicraft markets, though currently PMA registration is unavailable in Bali.

intel.whatItMeans: This covers the industrial refining and processing of crude oil into finished fuel products like gasoline, diesel, kerosene, jet fuel, and LPG. It’s large-scale downstream oil processing, turning raw petroleum into usable energy sources.
intel.baliReality: Even though this business field is fully open to foreign ownership at the national level, Bali currently applies a moratorium that blocks any foreign-owned company (PMA) from registering in this activity. The block is due to a local policy pausing low and medium-low risk business approvals for foreign investors, making it effectively closed in Bali for now.
intel.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur or company with heavy industrial experience, substantial capital, and access to crude oil supply chains, likely looking to set up a refinery outside of Bali or awaiting policy changes.
